recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Create a portrait-first browser canvas runner/platformer called **Neon Loop Rush**. Preserve the source loop: a player enters from a start screen, moves left/right, jumps only when grounded, lands on rectangular platforms, collects floating items worth +100, scrolls through procedurally generated platforms, fails by falling below the screen, and can restart. Reinterpret the experience as a Sonic-like neon arcade runner: a rebellious blue quill speedster named Blue Bolt dashes across glowing mag-rails, grabs gold rings, sparks speed particles, and races through a loop-heavy neon city. Use mobile-safe touch controls, readable HUD, bold comic typography, browser-native procedural canvas art, and no gameplay-rule changes.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source (`index_old.html`) is a mobile-friendly canvas runner/platformer. It starts at a menu, enters play on a button press, uses left/right horizontal movement with friction, permits jump only while grounded, applies gravity, collides the player with rectangular platforms, scrolls the camera, generates platforms ahead, awards 100 points for each floating collectible, triggers game over when the player falls below the screen, and restarts by reinitializing the same loop.

## Protected mechanics
- Input: keyboard arrows/space and touch/pointer buttons for left, right, and jump/boost.
- Movement: horizontal speed from `heroSpeed`, friction when no direction is pressed, vertical velocity from `jumpForce` and `gravity`.
- Collision: axis-aligned player/platform landing check with a small top-contact tolerance.
- Progression: procedural platforms spawn ahead as the camera advances and old platforms are culled.
- Scoring: each active collectible gives exactly +100 once.
- Failure/restart: falling below the viewport enters game-over state; retry reinitializes level and score.

## Remix blueprint
Reinterpret the same runner truth as **Neon Loop Rush**, a Sonic-inspired high-speed portrait runner starring Blue Bolt, a rebellious blue quill speedster crossing neon mag-rails. Platforms become mag-rails, floating collectibles become gold rings, procedural loop arches imply loop-heavy level design without adding new traversal rules, falling becomes a wipeout, and score becomes rings banked.

## Safe transformation surfaces
HUD vocabulary, title, typography, palette, player silhouette, ring drawing, platform treatment, background/parallax layers, particles, touch-control styling, start/game-over panels, and audio feedback are safe to transform because they do not alter gameplay semantics.
